summary: Six Rivers lookout built 1934 as a Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10-foot tower, staffed into the 1960s, now listed as gone; a 2008 post reported a radio tower on the site.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10 foot enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Lookout tower reported no longer there (2008 blog citing a book); the site then held a radio tower

staffing.status: last named lookout: Robert Tillitz of Chico, manning the site in 1965; no later staffing in the sources read

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Six Rivers National Forest

corrections.why: 213.4 m equals 700 ft, which matches the 700-foot plunge figure in the 1962 Taggart report rather than any tower height. FFLOS gives a 10-foot enclosed timber tower; the 1941 NGS description says the lookout is about 25 feet high, so 3.0 m covers only the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLA lists the site as gone and FFLOS says the removal date is unknown. The 2008 blog reports a book saying the lookout tower is gone. The OpenStreetMap entry carries building, fire_lookout and name tags with no status, so it does not show a standing tower. Treated as gone.

FFLOS gives a 10-foot enclosed timber tower under a cabin; the 1941 NGS description says the whole lookout is about 25 feet high. The two may measure different parts of the structure, so the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: No source after the 2008 blog describes the site, and none says whether the public may visit. The brief's height_m of 213.4 matches the 700-foot plunge figure in the 1962 report, so it is proposed for correction. The brief's osm=standing conflict is a misreading: the OSM way carries no status. Newspaper items are read second-hand through the Forest Lookouts page; the originals were not checked. FFLOS credits a USFS/Siskiyou County Museum photo, but no image URL was found, so no photo entry was added.
